ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of semicircle O, D is the midpoint of BC, extending OD intersects the arc $BC$ at point E, and point F is a point on the extension of OD such that $\angle B = \angle F$. CF is a tangent to the circle $O$; if AB = 4, $\angle B = 30^\circ$, connect AD, find the length of AD.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Join AD,\\
$\because$ AB is the diameter of semicircle $O$,\\
$\therefore \angle ACB=90^\circ$.\\
$\because$ AB$=4$, and $\angle B=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ AC$=2$, and $BC=\sqrt{4^2-2^2}=2\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ CD$=\sqrt{3}$,\\
In $\triangle ACD$, $AD=\sqrt{2^2+(\sqrt{3})^2}=\boxed{\sqrt{7}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a semicircle with AB as diameter, A at the left endpoint, B at the right endpoint, and O on AB as the center of the circle. Point C is on the semicircular arc, and AC and BC are connected. Point D is located on segment BC; an oblique line starting from O passes through D, continues to intersect arc BC at E, and then extends outward to F. CF is also drawn in the figure, tangent to the semicircle at C. It is required to connect AD and find AD; OD, E, F, and tangent CF in the figure are auxiliary structures and do not need to be used when calculating AD in this problem. Reasoning: Because AB is the diameter of semicircle O, and C is on the semicircle, by the theorem of an inscribed angle subtending a diameter, ∠ACB = 90°. Given AB = 4 and ∠ABC = 30°, therefore in right triangle ABC, AB is the hypotenuse, AC = AB·sin30° = 4 × 1/2 = 2, and BC = AB·cos30° = 4 × √3/2 = 2√3. Also because D is the midpoint of BC, CD = BC/2 = √3. Since AC ⟂ BC, and CD is on BC, AC ⟂ CD, so triangle ACD is a right triangle. By the Pythagorean theorem, AD = √(AC² + CD²) = √(2² + (√3)²) = √(4 + 3) = √7.
